To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed graphite, a new package for Bioconductor that converts pathway topology to gene networks, taking into account protein-protein interactions, chemical compounds and gene family members.
graphite is an R/Bioconordinator package able to provide gene-gene networks based on pathway databases.
graphite is the first R/Bioconducer package to convert the topology of pathways to gene networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for gene set analyses and the development of new packages to provide the required information.
the conversion of pathway topology into a gene network, which is an important and challenging task that allows topology-based gene set analysis.
developing a tool for pathway topology analysis that is able to provide a uniform resource of gene networks for topological gene set analysis.

graphite is a useful tool for pathway analysis.
graphite is an innovative and unique tool that provides a new and unique resource for the analysis of biological networks and gene sets.
the graphite package is a powerful and useful tool to convert pathway topology into gene/protein networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
graphite is an innovative and unique tool that provides a uniform representation of pathway information from four different resources.
graphite is a pathway network converter and a topological method provider.
graphite is a pathway database and a topological analysis provider.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of pathway topology is a powerful approach to identify genes and pathways that are relevant for specific phenotypes and diseases.
